objective: Test whether restoring R90's two-warp 128-value reduction geometry inside the one-program-per-row R94 kernel preserves accepted c1 arithmetic while retaining c2 batch invariance.

source_evidence.interpretation: R94 changed both row grouping and the within-row reduction tree. The two-warp arm isolates the reduction-tree mismatch while keeping one row per program.

treatment.change_from_r94: Set num_warps=2 for the fixed 128-wide row-stable gated RMSNorm kernel.
unchanged: R94 float32 arithmetic and output dtype
VLLM_XPU_GDN_ROW_STABLE_RMSNORM=1 for every Qwen GDN call

fixed_workload.sequence: Run cache-c000 alone at c1, then cache-c000 plus index-c001 at c2 on one fresh server and empty compile cache.

followup_if_pass: Build a non-tracing image and repeat c1/c2, then perform a clean-boot full varied-prompt qualification before performance measurement.
followup_if_fail: Preserve the result. If it restores c1 but loses c2, split the generated reduction and pointwise geometry exactly; if it retains R94, the pointwise or kernel split is also causally relevant.
promotion_boundary: Diagnostic only. No public speed or quality authority; the current boot contains an earlier GPU reset.
